about: Major deserts at their present-day extent, painted in the same sand as the Sahara. The Sahara itself is NOT here: it has its own field and its own Green Sahara toggle.

sourced.extent: Natural Earth 10m geography regions (public domain); the named polygons in each field, unedited.
sourced.margin_fade: Beyer, R.M., Krapp, M. & Manica, A. (2020). High-resolution terrestrial climate, bioclimate and vegetation for the last 120,000 years. Scientific Data 7, 236. doi:10.1038/s41597-020-0552-1. CC BY 4.0. Present-day BIOME4 class at 0.5 degrees, used to weight each cell so that semi-arid ground inside a generous polygon is not painted as sand.
sourced.mojave: US Environmental Protection Agency, Level III Ecoregions of the Conterminous United States, 2013-04-16, ecoregion "Mojave Basin and Range". Originator: US Environmental Protection Agency; access constraints None; use constraints None, with acknowledgement of the EPA requested. Public domain, 17 U.S.C. 105. Natural Earth has no Mojave polygon at all, so this one boundary comes from a second federal source rather than being hand-drawn; it is reprojected from USA Contiguous Albers Equal Area Conic to WGS84 and otherwise unaltered, and it takes the same margin fade as every other polygon here.

drawn: The 0.6 degree blur on every edge, and the weights given to the part-desert biome classes: 12=0.15, 13=0.45, 14=0.45, 19=0.25, 20=0.30, 21=1.00, 27=0.75, with a floor of 0.12 inside the polygon. A drawing, not a reconstruction.
not_drawn: The Sahara (its own field). Dune fields are not distinguished from stony desert. The Central Asian and Iranian deserts (Garagum, Qizilqum, Betpaqdala, Kavir, Lut, Margo, Rigestan), the Danakil, the Chalbi, the Negev and the Caatingas are in the source and are not drawn, because the ruling named nine regions and these are not among them. The Mojave IS drawn, from the EPA ecoregion above, because Natural Earth has no Mojave polygon and a hand-drawn one was ruled out.
